# netbird_user (Resource)

Invite and Manage Users, see [NetBird Docs](https://docs.netbird.io/how-to/add-users-to-your-network) for more information, existing users should be imported.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netbird_group" "example" {
  name = "Test"
}

resource "netbird_user" "service_user" {
  is_service_user = true
  name            = "Test"
  auto_groups     = [netbird_group.example.id]
  is_blocked      = false
  role            = "admin"
}

resource "netbird_user" "real_user" {
  is_service_user = false
  name            = "John Doe"
  email           = "johndoe@company.co"
  auto_groups     = [netbird_group.example.id]
  is_blocked      = false
  role            = "admin"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `auto_groups` (List of String) Group IDs to auto-assign to peers registered by this user
- `email` (String) User Email. NetBird does not change a user's email: a change is refused at plan time, or by the apply before it writes when the value is known only then.
- `is_blocked` (Boolean) If set to true then user is blocked and can't use the system
- `is_service_user` (Boolean) If set to true, creates a Service Account User. Left out, a new user is a regular user and an existing one keeps what it is, as for an imported identity provider user. NetBird does not change a user's kind, so a change is refused; declare a new `netbird_user` of the other kind and remove the old one.
- `name` (String) User Name. NetBird does not change a user's name, so a change is refused at plan time (or by the apply before it writes, for a value known only then); for a service user under a new name, declare a new `netbird_user` (with new tokens) and remove the old one. A new regular user is an invitation and needs `name` and `email`.
- `role` (String) User's NetBird account role (owner|admin|user|billing_admin|auditor|network_admin).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of a user
- `is_current` (Boolean) Set to true if the caller user is the same as the resource user
- `issued` (String) User issue method
- `last_login` (String) User Last Login timedate
- `status` (String) User status (active, invited or blocked)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import netbird_user.example user_id

# For example

terraform import netbird_user.example 2fd8f4d6-d6c2-44c3-b7a4-adb644177b3d
```
